learn.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
learn.headline: CoworkOS: a runtime that keeps long agent tasks on track
learn.reason: Shows how a model's decisions separate from runtime state in agent loops.

card.headline: Researchers build a system to help AI helpers handle long work
card.gist: A research team built CoworkOS, a frame around an AI model, called a harness. The model decides what to do. The harness keeps files, progress and logs, so work can resume after a stop.
card.picture: Think of an ETL scheduler and the engineer using it. The engineer decides which jobs run and checks the results. The scheduler keeps job state and logs, so a failed run can restart.
card.why_you: When you build agent loops, you must decide what the model handles and what your code tracks. This paper is one clear example of that split.
card.remember: The model decides; the harness remembers and keeps the work running.
card.term_meaning: The code around an AI model that runs its actions, keeps state and feeds results back to it.
card.say_it: I separate the agent's decisions from execution: the model picks actions, the harness keeps state and feedback.
card.follow_up_why: Because long tasks get interrupted, and the model alone cannot reliably store files, decisions and logs across sessions.
card.reality_check: The results come from the paper's own authors, not an independent test; the source does not say if code is released.
card.try_it: Give Claude Code a three-step task, then list what it tracked itself versus what it saved in files.
